text:
Jake Guentzel has 13 goals and 13 assists in 21 games, and his workload just went up: he's played 2.3 more minutes a night over his last 10 games, with Brandon Hagel day-to-day (Daily Faceoff). He answered with two goals against Washington on Tuesday, after a stretch CBS Sports tallied at ten points in five games.

The goals are ahead of the chances. He has 13 on 8.9 expected, shooting 22% against 17% last season, and Tampa has scored 9.1 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Both numbers usually come back toward normal. Our range for his season is 35 to 52 goals, which says the process supports a big year even after the cooling.

What he does well hasn't changed since Pittsburgh: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 6.2 scoring chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season (81st percentile) and taking plenty of shots off passes across the slot, the kind that go in about a quarter of the time. Evolving-Hockey noted his teammates rated in the 90th percentile, which flatters anyone's on-ice numbers. Watch whether the extra minutes keep his chance rate up without Hagel beside the play.
headline: Guentzel is filling the Hagel-sized gap
